title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Recovery, Resilience, and Self-Reliance - Transition to Self-Sufficiency in Western CAR programme will work in Ombella M'Poko and Lobaye prefectures, Central African Republic. It aims to contribute to Concern Central African Republic’s Food Systems for Food Security thematic programme, and the goal of the programme is to ensure sustainable increase in food and nutrition security levels of households at increased risk of shocks. The programme will support over 131,520 people living in extreme poor households, including female, headed households, households with disabled members and internally displaced people. This will be done through increased crop production and diversification, stronger access to market and economic opportunities for poor and vulnerable people, improved access to business knowledge and skills and improved access to finance.. RM Adaptation 2: Climate-smart agriculture and associated activities, such as Integrated Soil Fertility Management, organic fertilisers, post-harvest handling, and vegetable gardening, are is fundamental to the purpose of this outcome and an eligible area of work for Rio Marker's scoring of two under adaptation, as per Rio Marker Handbook: Agriculture CRS score 311 p.22 - Sustainable climate-resilient farming methods (adaptation score 2). CSA activities improve the resilience of individuals and communities to climate change through reducing the vulnerability and exposure of farming systems to slow-onset (e.g., reduced rainfall, shifting seasonal patterns, etc.) and rapid (e.g., flooding, storms, drought) climate risks. CSA does this by promoting activities that improves farmer’s knowledge and skills of when various plant species are most sensitive to weather or climate events in order to identify potential risks related to climate change and to select context appropriate adaptive management practices that they can use to avoid or reduce risk exposure. DRR 1: By working on hunger and nutrition within sustainable food systems and climate smart agriculture, this outcome builds resilience of households and communities, ultimately reducing humanitarian needs sustainably. Aid to the environment 1: CSA and landscape management approaches promoted under the FS4FS support the protection of natural resources. Capacity Building 1: There are a range capacity building activities in this outcome e.g. participatory farmer-led approaches, government and private extension services, farmer groups/ associations, pastoral systems, and natural resource management; post-harvest management; processing, packaging and marketing of (new) food products, storage and transport. Gender Equality 1: Direct implementation of gender and protection activities is fundamental to all activities Nutrition 1: This outcome focuseson increased crop production and diversification, thus improving the nutritional status of HHS.
